data.segment_description:
(Studio: Katie Couric)  Stock Market Report.  

(Washington: Bob Orr)  The slow progress towards a government rescue plan for the nation's financial system examined; details given of the politicians' reaction to the 700-billion dollar bailout proposal and of the executive compensation and foreclosure issues.  [Treasury Secretary Henry PAULSON&nbsp- says the taxpayers are on the hook; talks about helping homeowners and stimulating the economy.]  [Federal Reserve Board chairman Ben BERNANKE&nbsp- outlines the possible economic impact.]  [Senators Christopher DODD, Richard SHELBY, Representative Mike PENCE&nbsp- comment on the issue.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  Report introduced.  

(New York: Anthony Mason)  The money game in the bailout examined; details given about the bad mortgage-backed securities and the recent securities sale by Merrill Lynch.  [Tavakoli Structured Finance Janet TAVAKOLI†- comments on the complicated finances.]  [University of Maryland Peter CRAMTON†- talks about the banks.]  The government help in the 1980s savings and loan crisis recalled.

(Studio: Katie Couric)  The discussion of the American financial crisis at the U.N. noted; scenes shown of President Bush, who also criticizes Russia and Iran; details given of the statement from Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad about his country's nuclear program and the US.  [AHMADINEJAD - {thru translator} says the American empire is reaching the end of the road.]   (Pentagon: David Martin)  Iran's atomic program featured; Iran government photos of a secret uranium enrichment plant shown; details given about how many centrifuges and enrichment plants Iran may have.  [Analyst David ALBRIGHT - analyzes the photos showing how far along is the Iranian program.]

(Studio: Katie Couric)  A shooting massacre at a trade school in Kaukajoki,† Finland, reported; scenes shown.   (London: Sheila MacVicar)  This second school shooting in a small town in Finland by an armed gunman featured; scenes shown of his Internet video and from outside the school; details given about the gun laws.

(Studio: Katie Couric)  Report introduced.  

(New York: Jon LaPook)  A new study on the survival of cardiac arrest examined; details given about the timetable for help indicating the importance of location; statistics by city cited; details given about the reasons for the success rate in Seattle.  [New York Presbyterian Hospital Dr. Lori MOSCA†- says survival is different depending on where you live; comments on the community's emergency medical system.]
(Studio: Katie Couric)  The release of methane gas in the Arctic Ocean that could speed up global warming reported; diagrams shown.
(Studio: Katie Couric)  The announcement by seven Western states and four Canadian provinces of the pooling of efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions reported.

(Studio: Katie Couric)  Series report introduced.  

(Fresno: John Blackstone)  Where presidential candidates Senators John McCain and Barack Obama stand on the issue of climate change examined; scenes shown of the Adelie penguins of Antarctica, which has been losing ice through global warming and from California where methane is being rerouted from cows to produce electricity.  [Penguin researcher/teacher Jean PENNYCOOK†- says the penguins cannot survive if the Antarctica ice goes away.]  [Near Modesto, dairy farmer John \FISCALINI%- talks about his cows, their methane and his new machine.]  What each candidate says about environmental measures to curtail greenhouse emissions noted; details given about the cap and trade approach to emissions and how the two plans do differ.  [McCAIN, OBAMA - talk about reducing gases, the cap and trade option for the energy economy and how the steps will require hardship.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  Thursday's segment in the series previewed.
(Studio: Katie Couric)  Republican vice presidential candidate Governor Sarah Palin shown meeting with Afghanistan's President Hamid Karzai.

(Studio: Katie Couric)  The response of presidential candidates Senators John McCain and Barack Obama to the questions "when is it appropriate to lie" and "what is your favorite movie" presented.  [OBAMA&nbsp- says you cannot lie to the American people, though you can put out a hypothetical; comments on the "soft lie" in the culture of Washington.]  [McCAIN&nbsp- says a president has to have credibility, though a scenario could possibly be drawn.]  [McCAIN&nbsp- explains why "Viva Zapata" is his favorite movie that is an heroic tale of sacrifice; recounts his favorite scene.]  [OBAMA&nbsp- explains why the "Godfather" saga is his favorite with the opening scene of the first film his favorite.]

(Studio: Katie Couric)  Report introduced.   (Washington: Nancy Cordes)  How states have personality traits examined; details given about how New York staters are neurotic.  [New York resident Gary PAUL†, Los Angeles resident John DONLEY†- comment.]  [University of Cambridge Peter Jason RENTFROW†- says places can effect one's physical health.]  Map shown of the "stress belt" running from New York to Louisiana that has higher death rates from cancer, heart disease and stroke, "conscientiousness" in the Southwest, "extraversion" in the Midwest and "openness" on the West coast.
